steps.label: One update moves this sample in the right direction · 1
steps.speakerNotes: Substitute the weight update into the new inner product. The added term is learning rate times error times squared input norm. The rate is positive and the constant input makes the squared norm at least one. The error therefore determines direction, not immediate correction or improvement on other samples.

steps.label: Finite convergence needs linearly separable data · 1
steps.speakerNotes: Linear separability means a line can perfectly separate these two-dimensional classes. The standard single-sample Perceptron converges after finitely many updates on separable data. Repeated passes on nonseparable data cannot meet a zero-error stopping rule; an implementation may still impose a pass limit.

steps.label: From zero, a positive learning rate only scales the weights · 1
steps.speakerNotes: This scaling result requires zero initialization, a constant positive rate, identical sample order, and the same convention at zero. All sixteen visits were checked: rate two gives twice the weights and identical predictions. This is not a claim about learning rates in all models.

steps.label: A batch sums the corrections before one update · 1
steps.speakerNotes: A batch evaluates all outputs and errors under the same old weights, sums the correction terms, and updates once. Sequential processing can change weights between samples, so a multi-sample batch generally differs from sequential updates. A batch of one reduces directly to the single-sample rule.
